'''NewsGuard''' is a rating system for news and information websites. It is accessible via [[browser extension]]s and [[Mobile app|mobile apps]]. It rates the websites' trustworthiness on a scale of 0 to 100, based on whether they adhere to editorial and journalistic standards.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 February 2025 |title=Have you tried NewsGuard yet? |url=https://blogs.eui.eu/library/have-you-tried-newsguard-yet |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251219235548/https://blogs.eui.eu/library/have-you-tried-newsguard-yet |archive-date=19 December 2025 |access-date=19 Dec 2025 |website=[[European University Institute]] Library blog}}</ref> NewsGuard Technologies Inc., the company behind the tool, also provides services such as [[misinformation]] tracking and [[brand safety]] for advertisers, search engines, social media platforms, cybersecurity firms, and government agencies.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Mayhew|first=Freddy|date=2019-10-29|title=News websites rated 'red' by Newsguard could miss out on ad money after agency deal|url=https://www.pressgazette.co.uk/news-websites-rated-red-by-newsguard-could-miss-out-on-ad-money-after-agency-deal/|access-date=2021-02-16|website=Press Gazette|language=en-US|archive-date=January 26, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126215353/https://pressgazette.co.uk/news-websites-rated-red-by-newsguard-could-miss-out-on-ad-money-after-agency-deal/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=NSIN Post {{!}} NSIN {{!}} #52Weeks: Countering Disinformation|url=https://innovatedefense.net/nsin/customObject/viewCustomObject/ba2a2be0e2af|access-date=2021-02-16|website=UNUM|language=en|archive-date=November 29, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201129005834/https://innovatedefense.net/nsin/customObject/viewCustomObject/ba2a2be0e2af|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== History ==
NewsGuard Technologies was founded in 2018 by [[Steven Brill (journalist)|Steven Brill]] and [[L. Gordon Crovitz]], who serve as co-CEOs.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://money.cnn.com/2018/03/04/media/newsguard-steven-brill-gordon-crovitz/index.html|title=This start-up wants to evaluate your news sources|last=Stelter|first=Brian|authorlink=Brian Stelter|work=[[CNN Business]]|date=March 4, 2018|access-date=January 23, 2019|archive-date=June 11, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200611184201/https://money.cnn.com/2018/03/04/media/newsguard-steven-brill-gordon-crovitz/index.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Crovitz was a former publisher of ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]''.<ref name="Fortinsky-2024">{{Cite web |last=Fortinsky |first=Sarah |date=2024-06-13 |title=James Comer investigating news-rating group NewsGuard |url=https://thehill.com/media/4721552-newsguard-probe-oversight-committee/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240808215737/https://thehill.com/media/4721552-newsguard-probe-oversight-committee/ |archive-date=August 8, 2024 |access-date=2024-08-08 |website=The Hill |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2018, [[Joyce Purnick]], former bureau chief and editor at ''[[The New York Times]]'', and Amy Westfeldt, an editor with the [[Associated Press]] for 25 years, joined Newsguard.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Calderone |first1=Michael |title=Fox-run state? — Harper's editor fired — NewsGuard expands — Tampa Bay Times cuts — Katy Perry wants WaPo |url=https://www.politico.com/media/newsletters/morning-media/2018/04/19/fox-run-state-harpers-editor-fired-newsguard-expands-katy-perry-wants-wapo-001495/ |work=Politico |date=2018-04-19 |access-date=July 8, 2024 |archive-date=July 8, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240708183921/https://www.politico.com/media/newsletters/morning-media/2018/04/19/fox-run-state-harpers-editor-fired-newsguard-expands-katy-perry-wants-wapo-001495/ |url-status=live }}</ref> NewsGuard expanded its coverage to news in European languages such as French and German ahead of the [[2019 European Parliament election]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Maurer |first=Jacob |date=22 February 2019 |title=A certifier for media credibility? |url=https://www.sueddeutsche.de/medien/newsguard-fake-news-medienkompetenz-1.4336597 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306044440/https://www.sueddeutsche.de/medien/newsguard-fake-news-medienkompetenz-1.4336597 |archive-date=March 6, 2019 |access-date=2019-03-02 |work=[[Süddeutsche Zeitung]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=June 6, 2019 |title=NewsGuard's "news trust" ratings rolled out to Europe |url=https://en.ejo.ch/ethics-quality/newsguards-news-trust-ratings-rolled-out-to-europe |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20190906105932/https://en.ejo.ch/ethics-quality/newsguards-news-trust-ratings-rolled-out-to-europe |archive-date=September 6, 2019 |publisher=[[European Journalism Observatory]] |language=en}}</ref>

In April 2019, the co-founders of NewsGuard announced that they had entered talks with British [[Internet service provider|internet service providers]] to incorporate their credibility scoring system into consumer internet packages. Under the plans, a user would see a warning message before visiting a misleading site without needing to have the NewsGuard extension installed. Users would also have the ability to disable the feature.<ref name="Waterson-2019">{{Cite news |last=Waterson |first=Jim |date=2019-04-24 |title=Untrustworthy news sites could be flagged automatically in UK |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2019/apr/24/untrustworthy-news-sites-could-be-flagged-automatically-in-uk |access-date=2019-12-31 |issn=0261-3077 |archive-date=July 3, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240703131308/https://www.theguardian.com/media/2019/apr/24/untrustworthy-news-sites-could-be-flagged-automatically-in-uk |url-status=live }}</ref>

In January 2020, NewsGuard began notifying users that it would become a paid, member-supported browser extension in early 2020, while remaining free for libraries and schools. Early adopters received a 33% discount on the price, paying $1.95/month (USD) or £1.95/month (UK).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayhew |first=Freddy |date=2020-01-09 |title=News website rating tool Newsguard to start charging for service |url=https://pressgazette.co.uk/news-website-rating-tool-newsguard-start-charging-service-paid-membership/ |access-date=2020-01-21 |website=Press Gazette |language=en-US |archive-date=January 9, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200109182944/https://www.pressgazette.co.uk/news-website-rating-tool-newsguard-start-charging-service-paid-membership/ |url-status=live }}</ref> NewsGuard launched in Australia and New Zealand in March 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mumbrella.com.au/credibility-ratings-platform-newsguard-launches-locally-779556|title=Credibility ratings platform NewsGuard launches locally|date=March 15, 2023|website=[[Mumbrella]]|last=Welch|first=Kalila}}</ref> As of 2025, they offer reliability scores of news sources on web, social media, and mobile platforms.<ref>{{Cite web |title=News Reliability Ratings |url=https://www.newsguardtech.com/solutions/news-reliability-ratings/ |access-date=18 Dec 2025 |website=NewsGuard Tech}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Welcome to NewsGuard |url=https://www.newsguardtech.com/welcome-to-newsguard/ |access-date=18 Dec 2025 |website=NewsGuard Tech}}</ref>

== Company structure and business model ==
NewsGuard is based in [[New York City]].<ref name="Perlow-2020b" /> It raised $6 million in 2018.<ref name="Stelter-2022">{{Cite web |last=Stelter |first=Brian |date=2022-01-16 |title=A startup that rates the reliability of news sources says it's making a profit |url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/01/16/media/newsguard-startup-profit-expands/index.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240628052924/https://www.cnn.com/2022/01/16/media/newsguard-startup-profit-expands/index.html |archive-date=June 28, 2024 |access-date=2024-08-08 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref> Investors include the [[Knight Foundation]], [[Publicis]], and former [[Reuters]] executive [[Tom Glocer]].<ref name="Lee-2019">{{cite news|last=Lee|first=Edmund|title=Veterans of the News Business Are Now Fighting Fakes|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/01/16/business/media/media-steve-brill-fake-news.html|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=January 16, 2019|access-date=January 23, 2019|archive-date=May 17, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200517033803/https://www.nytimes.com/2019/01/16/business/media/media-steve-brill-fake-news.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Li|first=Kenneth|title=NewsGuard's 'real news' seal of approval helps spark change in fake news era|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-media-newsguard/newsguards-real-news-seal-of-approval-helps-spark-change-in-fake-news-era-idUSKCN1PQ5FV|work=[[Reuters]]|date=February 1, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019|archive-date=April 27, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190427053405/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-media-newsguard/newsguards-real-news-seal-of-approval-helps-spark-change-in-fake-news-era-idUSKCN1PQ5FV|url-status=live}}</ref> Its advisors include former officials such as [[Tom Ridge]] (former [[Secretary of Homeland Security]]), [[Richard Stengel]] (former [[Under Secretary of State for Public Diplomacy and Public Affairs]]), [[Michael Hayden (general)|Michael Hayden]] (former [[Director of the CIA]]), [[Anders Fogh Rasmussen]] (former [[Secretary General of NATO]]), and [[Wikipedia]] founder [[Jimmy Wales]].<ref name="Lapowski-2018" /><ref name="Waterson-2019" /> For revenue, NewsGuard Technologies licenses their ratings. Clients include technology companies and the advertising industry, who view the ratings as a way to protect clients against advertising on sites that could harm their brand.<ref name="Lee-2019" /> In January 2022, the company said it was profitable, having doubled its revenue over the previous year.<ref name="Stelter-2022" />

== Products and services ==
As of 2019, the company employed 35 journalists to review over 2,000 news sites. Ratings are broken down in terms of reliability, trustworthiness, and financial conflict of interest. This and additional information is then displayed in the form of a "Nutrition Label" by the NewsGuard [[browser extension]] whenever a user visits a news site. Sites that pass are shown with a green icon next to their name. Those with low scores are shown with a red icon. Research has shown that readers who see the green icon find the corresponding news site more accurate and trustworthy compared to those who see no icon or a red icon.<ref name="Lapowski-2018">{{cite web |last=Lapowski |first=Issie |date=August 23, 2018 |title=NewsGuard Wants to Fight Fake News With Humans, Not Algorithms |url=https://www.wired.com/story/newsguard-extension-fake-news-trust-score/ |access-date=January 23, 2019 |work=[[Wired.com]] |archive-date=April 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190403185552/https://www.wired.com/story/newsguard-extension-fake-news-trust-score/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Morgan |first=David |date=March 5, 2018 |title=New venture aims to combat "fake news" on social media with warning labels |work=[[CBS News]] |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/new-venture-will-help-combat-fake-news-on-social-media-with-warning-labels/ |access-date=January 23, 2019 |archive-date=January 24, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190124041525/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/new-venture-will-help-combat-fake-news-on-social-media-with-warning-labels/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Brill positions the extension as an alternative to government regulation and automated algorithms, such as those used by [[Facebook]].<ref name="Lapowski-2018" /> NewsGuard attempts to advise sites that it labels as unreliable on how to come into compliance with its rating criteria.<ref>{{cite news |last=Atkinson |first=Claire |date=August 24, 2018 |title=NewsGuard gives Fox News a thumbs up, Breitbart a thumbs down |work=[[NBC News]] |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/card/newsguard-gives-fox-news-thumbs-breitbart-thumbs-down-n903726 |access-date=January 23, 2019 |archive-date=January 24, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190124104826/https://www.nbcnews.com/card/newsguard-gives-fox-news-thumbs-breitbart-thumbs-down-n903726 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Supported systems===

NewsGuard operates a consumer-facing browser extension,<ref name="Perlow-2020b">{{Cite web |last=Perlow |first=Jason |date=March 24, 2020 |title=NewsGuard drops its paywall to combat coronavirus misinformation |url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/newsguard-drops-its-paywall-to-combat-coronavirus-information/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201126210224/https://www.zdnet.com/article/newsguard-drops-its-paywall-to-combat-coronavirus-information/ |archive-date=November 26, 2020 |access-date=2021-02-16 |website=ZDNet |language=en}}</ref> as well as [[Mobile app|mobile apps]] for [[iOS]] and [[Android (operating system)|Android]].<ref name="Perlow-2020a">{{Cite web |last=Perlow |first=Jason |date=May 14, 2020 |title=NewsGuard becomes free for all Microsoft Edge users |url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/newsguard-becomes-free-for-all-microsoft-edge-users/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210121025442/https://www.zdnet.com/article/newsguard-becomes-free-for-all-microsoft-edge-users/ |archive-date=January 21, 2021 |access-date=2021-02-16 |website=ZDNet |language=en}}</ref> Supported browsers for the extension include [[Google Chrome]], [[Microsoft Edge]], [[Firefox]], and [[Safari (web browser)|Safari]]. It is free of charge for Microsoft Edge users.<ref name="Perlow-2020a" />

== Ratings ==
NewsGuard's team of journalists and editors rate websites based on the following criteria:<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Website Rating Process and Criteria |url=https://www.newsguardtech.com/ratings/rating-process-criteria/ |access-date=19 Dec 2025 |website=NewsGuard Tech}}</ref>

# "Does not repeatedly publish false or egregiously misleading content."
# "Gathers and presents information responsibly."
# "Has effective practices for correcting errors."
# "Handles the difference between news and opinion responsibly."
# "Avoids deceptive headlines."
# "Website discloses ownership and financing."
# "Clearly labels advertising."
# "Reveals who's in charge, including possible conflicts of interest."
# "The site provides the names of content creators, along with either contact or biographical information."

They clarify that a site rating above 75% indicates credibility, a site rating of 60-75% indicates "credibility with exceptions", and a site rating below 60% indicates unreliability; the ratings are explained in depth in each site's "Nutrition Label".<ref name=":0" /> Their founders cautioned that the "Nutrition Labels" should not be treated as an endorsement equivalent to the [[Nutrition facts label#United States|nutrition facts label]] from the [[Food and Drug Administration]].<ref name="Lee-2019" /> As of January 2021, NewsGuard said it has rated more than 6,000 news sites that account for 95% of online engagement with news in the U.S., the U.K., France, Germany and Italy.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 6, 2020 |title=Startups battle the spread of fake news during the pandemic {{!}} PitchBook |url=https://pitchbook.com/news/articles/how-startups-are-battling-the-spread-of-fake-news-during-the-pandemic |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200922142247/https://pitchbook.com/news/articles/how-startups-are-battling-the-spread-of-fake-news-during-the-pandemic |archive-date=September 22, 2020 |access-date=2021-02-16 |website=pitchbook.com |language=en}}</ref> In 2022, a study from the [[NYU]] Center for Social Media and Politics found that, although NewsGuard ratings did not noticeably reduce the popularity of unreliable news sources, they encouraged the most frequent consumers of misinformation to read more reliable news sources.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Aslett |first=Kevin |date=6 May 2022 |title=News credibility labels have limited average effects on news diet quality and fail to reduce misperceptions |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.abl3844 |journal=[[Science Advances]] |volume=8 |issue=18 |doi=10.1126/sciadv.abl3844 |via=Science.org|pmc=9075792 }}</ref>

=== Examples ===
As of March 2023, ''[[The Guardian Australia]]'', [[ABC News Australia]], and ''[[The Australian]]'' had scored 100/100 when NewsGuard launched in Australia.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Buckley |first=John |date=March 15, 2023 |title=News Corp's the Oz gets full marks for 'credibility and transparency' from misinformation firm in local launch |url=https://www.crikey.com.au/2023/03/15/news-corps-the-australian-credibility-transparency-newsguard/ |website=[[Crikey]]}}</ref> As of June 2024, the service rated [[Fox News]] at 69.5, ''[[Breitbart News]]'' at 49.5, ''[[The New Republic]]'' at 92.5, ''[[Mother Jones (magazine)|Mother Jones]]'' at 69.5, and ''[[The Washington Post]]'' at 100.<ref name="Wagner-2024">{{Cite news |last=Wagner |first=Laura |date=June 30, 2024 |title=A lifelong media maven grapples with the misinformation crisis |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/style/media/2024/06/30/steven-brill-death-of-truth/ |newspaper=The Washington Post}}</ref> In 2024, it downgraded ''The New York Times'' from 100 to 87.5 for not distinguishing clearly enough between opinion and fact.<ref name="Wagner-2024" /> As of December 2024, NewsGuard rated [[Newsmax]] and [[One America News Network]] at 20.<ref name="Oremus-2024" /> The company issues corrections for erroneous ratings. When ''[[MailOnline]]'' objected to being listed as unreliable,<ref name="BBC News-2019">{{cite news |date=2019-01-23 |title=Daily Mail demands browser warning U-turn |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-46976834 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190123164756/https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-46976834 |archive-date=January 23, 2019 |access-date=2019-01-23 |work=[[BBC News]]}}</ref> NewsGuard admitted they were wrong on some counts, and the decision to list ''MailOnline'' as unreliable was reversed in 2019.<ref>{{cite news |last=Walker |first=James |title='We were wrong': US news rating tool boosts Mail Online trust ranking after talks with unnamed Daily Mail exec |url=https://www.pressgazette.co.uk/we-were-wrong-us-news-rating-tool-boosts-mail-online-trust-ranking-after-talks-with-unnamed-daily-mail-exec/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190212062704/https://pressgazette.co.uk/we-were-wrong-us-news-rating-tool-boosts-mail-online-trust-ranking-after-talks-with-unnamed-daily-mail-exec/ |archive-date=February 12, 2019 |access-date=17 January 2020 |publisher=[[Press Gazette]]}}</ref>

=== Disinformation in AI ===
NewsGuard has audited the output of various AI models to identify disinformation. When ''The New York Times'' replicated their experiment in 2023, they found that [[ChatGPT]] offered disinformation in its responses 33% of the time.<ref>{{Cite web |date=Feb 8, 2023 |title=Disinformation Researchers Raise Alarms About A.I. Chatbots |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/02/08/technology/ai-chatbots-disinformation.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250801185942/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/02/08/technology/ai-chatbots-disinformation.html |archive-date=1 August 2025 |access-date=17 Dec 2025 |website=New York Times}}</ref> NewsGuard later found that [[DeepSeek]]'s output was considerably more likely to produce disinformation, at an 83% failure rate.<ref>{{Cite web |date=Jan 29, 2025 |title=DeepSeek's chatbot achieves 17% accuracy, trails Western rivals in NewsGuard audit |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/china/deepseeks-chatbot-achieves-17-accuracy-trails-western-rivals-newsguard-audit-2025-01-29/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250130030254/https://www.reuters.com/world/china/deepseeks-chatbot-achieves-17-accuracy-trails-western-rivals-newsguard-audit-2025-01-29/ |archive-date=30 January 2025 |access-date=17 Dec 2025 |website=Reuters}}</ref> In August 2025, they found that leading generative AI tools repeat false news claims 35% of the time on average.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Constantino |first=Tor |date=Sep 5, 2025 |title=AI Chatbots Now Get The News Wrong 1 Out Of 3 Times |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/torconstantino/2025/09/05/ai-chatbots-now-get-the-news-wrong-1-out-of-3-times/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250911094151/https://www.forbes.com/sites/torconstantino/2025/09/05/ai-chatbots-now-get-the-news-wrong-1-out-of-3-times/ |archive-date=11 September 2025 |website=[[Forbes]]}}</ref> NewsGuard also audited [[Sora (text-to-video model)|Sora 2]] and found that it produced videos advancing fake claims in 80% of cases.<ref>{{Cite web |date=28 Oct 2025 |title=Disinfo Update 28/10/2025 |url=https://www.disinfo.eu/disinfo-update-28-10-2025-2-2-2/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251218015125/https://www.disinfo.eu/disinfo-update-28-10-2025-2-2-2/ |archive-date=18 December 2025 |website=EU Disinfo Lab}}</ref> According to NewsGuard, [[Russian propaganda]] networks are attempting to "infect" [[Large language model|large language models]] by spamming fake news, so that they will output more [[pro-Russia]] disinformation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fact check: How do I spot errors in AI chatbots? |url=https://www.dw.com/en/fact-check-how-do-i-spot-errors-in-ai-chatbots/a-72106646 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251218015512/https://www.dw.com/en/fact-check-how-do-i-spot-errors-in-ai-chatbots/a-72106646 |archive-date=18 December 2025 |access-date=18 Dec 2025 |website=[[Deutsche Welle]]}}</ref>
=== Russian disinformation ===
NewsGuard has researched Russian disinformation multiple times. In April 2025, the group uncovered a disinformation campaign by [[Storm-1516]] targeting [[France]], consisting of AI generated videos and fake news stories which were designed to incite [[Racism in Europe|racism]] and discredit French and Ukrainian leaders.<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 Apr 2025 |title=NewsGuard details a Russian disinformation campaign by Storm-1516 targeting France |url=https://incyber.org/en/article/newsguard-details-a-russian-disinformation-campaign-by-storm-1516-targeting-france/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251218221307/https://incyber.org/en/article/newsguard-details-a-russian-disinformation-campaign-by-storm-1516-targeting-france/ |archive-date=18 December 2025 |access-date=18 Dec 2025 |website=InCyber News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=7 May 2025 |title=Russia behind dozens of disinformation campaigns targeting Ukraine and allies, France says |url=https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20250507-russia-disinformation-france-ukraine |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250509102642/https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20250507-russia-disinformation-france-ukraine |archive-date=9 May 2025 |access-date=18 Dec 2025 |website=[[France 24]]}}</ref> Following the [[2025 Russia–United States summit]], NewsGuard found that Russian groups were spreading false rumors of a [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] assassin in [[Alaska]] and a potential [[cession]] of Alaska to Russia, and tracked the spread of the claims across social media.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Myers |first=Steven Lee |date=Aug 15, 2025 |title=False Flags, Fake Flags: Propaganda Muddles the Trump-Putin Meeting |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/15/world/europe/misinformation-russia.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250819100949/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/15/world/europe/misinformation-russia.html |archive-date=19 August 2025 |access-date=18 Dec 2025 |website=[[New York Times]]}}</ref> In September 2025, they found that [[Moldova]] was targeted by over 40 false narratives, with the goal of undermining President [[Maia Sandu]] and Moldova's potential [[EU accession]] ahead of parliamentary elections.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ilyushina |first=Mary |date=September 27, 2025 |title=E.U. and Russia battle over Moldova’s future as elections loom |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2025/09/27/moldova-elections-eu-russia/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250927070059/https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2025/09/27/moldova-elections-eu-russia/ |archive-date=27 September 2025 |access-date=18 Dec 2025 |website=[[Washington Post]]}}</ref>

== Criticism ==
In 2018, [[Joshua Benton]] wrote in the ''[[Columbia Journalism Review]]'' that NewsGuard is "trying to attack a real problem in misinformation; they’re doing interesting work that I enjoyed exploring. But the upside of this sort of labeling — a quick way to make a judgment at a glance — is in direct tension with the nuance modern [[media literacy]] requires."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Benton |first=Joshua |author-link=Joshua Benton |date=August 24, 2018 |title=NewsGuard considers Fox News a healthy part of your news diet |url=https://www.niemanlab.org/2018/08/newsguard-considers-fox-news-a-healthy-part-of-your-news-diet/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250315174154/https://www.niemanlab.org/2018/08/newsguard-considers-fox-news-a-healthy-part-of-your-news-diet/ |archive-date=March 15, 2025 |access-date=May 1, 2025 |website=Columbia Journalism Review}}</ref> In March 2025, the [[U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York]] dismissed a [[defamation]] lawsuit against NewsGuard by the Consortium for Independent Journalism (CIJ), the owner of the website ''[[Consortium News]]''. The ruling was that the CIJ did not make a sufficient showing that NewsGuard acted with [[actual malice]] in assessing the credibility of its journalism.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Judge throws out libel suit against media misinformation rating firm NewsGuard |url=https://www.courthousenews.com/judge-throws-out-libel-suit-against-media-misinformation-rating-firm-newsguard/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250403114627/https://www.courthousenews.com/judge-throws-out-libel-suit-against-media-misinformation-rating-firm-newsguard/ |archive-date=April 3, 2025 |access-date=2025-04-19 |website=[[Courthouse News]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Allegations of bias and censorship ===
NewsGuard's partnership with the AFT was criticized by [[American conservatives]] and [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]] politicians who said that NewsGuard ranked left-leaning media outlets higher than right-leaning ones, citing a study by the [[Media Research Center]] in 2021.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Flood |first1=Brian |date=1 June 2022 |title=Republican lawmakers demand answers about controversial AFT-NewsGuard anti-misinformation pact |url=https://www.foxnews.com/media/republican-aft-newsguard-misinformation-pact |work=Fox News |archive-date=December 22, 2024 |access-date=November 26, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241222145316/https://www.foxnews.com/media/republican-aft-newsguard-misinformation-pact |url-status=live }}</ref>{{Efn|In 2019 NewsGuard approved sites include ''[[The New York Times]]'', ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'', and [[BuzzFeed]].<ref name="Lee-2019" /> Sites labeled as unreliable include ''[[Breitbart News]]'',<ref>{{Cite web |last=Elliott |first=Matt |date=January 31, 2019 |title=Fake news spotter: How to enable Microsoft Edge's NewsGuard |url=https://www.cnet.com/tech/mobile/fake-news-spotter-how-to-enable-microsoft-edges-newsguard/ |access-date=2024-07-15 |website=[[CNET]] |language=en |archive-date=January 9, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230109225348/https://www.cnet.com/tech/mobile/fake-news-spotter-how-to-enable-microsoft-edges-newsguard/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[InfoWars]]'', the ''[[Daily Kos]]'', [[Sputnik (news agency)|Sputnik]],<ref name="BBC News-2019" /> [[RT (TV network)|RT]], [[WikiLeaks]],<ref name="Lee-2019" /> [[Fox News]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://pressgazette.co.uk/fox-news-newsguard/|title=Fox News 'fails to adhere to basic journalistic standards', says credibility rater Newsguard|work=[[Press Gazette]]|date=2022-07-21|access-date=2022-07-21|archive-date=July 22, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220722022534/https://pressgazette.co.uk/fox-news-newsguard/|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[The Epoch Times]]'',<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Perrone |first1=Alessio |last2=Loucaides |first2=Darren |date=2022-03-10 |title=A key source for Covid-skeptic movements, the Epoch Times yearns for a global audience |url=https://www.codastory.com/disinformation/epoch-times/ |access-date=2024-07-03 |website=[[Coda Media]] |language=en-US |archive-date=March 13, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220313044144/https://www.codastory.com/disinformation/epoch-times/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and [[Leading Report]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Summers |first=William |date=September 14, 2023 |title=Senator shares baseless claim linking vaccines to stillbirths |url=https://www.aap.com.au/factcheck/senator-shares-baseless-claim-linking-vaccines-to-stillbirths/ |access-date=2024-07-03 |website=[[Australian Associated Press]] |language=en |archive-date=January 11, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240111003401/https://www.aap.com.au/factcheck/senator-shares-baseless-claim-linking-vaccines-to-stillbirths/ |url-status=live }}</ref>}} In 2024, Republican [[House Oversight Committee]] chairman [[James Comer]] opened a probe into NewsGuard, accusing them of having an anti-conservative bias and demanding more details on their collaboration with government agencies.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Falconer |first=Rebecca |date=Jun 13, 2024 |title=House Republicans launch investigation into news rating group NewsGuard |url=https://www.axios.com/2024/06/14/newsguard-oversight-committee-investigation-free-speech |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241024115604/https://www.axios.com/2024/06/14/newsguard-oversight-committee-investigation-free-speech |archive-date=24 October 2024 |website=Axios}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Ted |date=December 19, 2024 |title=Attacking The Watchdog: How Media Rating Site NewsGuard Ended Up As A Target For GOP Lawmakers And Regulators |url=https://deadline.com/2024/12/newsguard-newsmax-trump-fcc-1236202249/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250919185305/https://deadline.com/2024/12/newsguard-newsmax-trump-fcc-1236202249/ |archive-date=19 September 2025 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref> In response, CEO [[L. Gordon Crovitz]] said, "Under NewsGuard's apolitical rating system, many conservative outlets outscore similar left-leaning brands: ''[[The Daily Caller]]'' outscores ''[[The Daily Beast]]'', the ''[[Daily Wire]]'' outscores the ''[[Daily Kos]]'', Fox News outscores [[MSNBC]] and ''The Wall Street Journal'' outscores the ''New York Times''."<ref name="Fortinsky-2024" />

In 2024, ''[[The Daily Wire]]'', ''[[The Federalist (website)|The Federalist]]'', and [[Texas]] attorney general [[Ken Paxton]] sued the [[Department of State]], arguing that providing a $25,000 grant to NewsGuard was funding technology that censored right-leaning news outlets.<ref name="Tani-2024" /><ref name="Raymond-2024">{{Cite news |last=Raymond |first=Nate |date=May 8, 2024 |title=Texas' lawsuit claiming US helped censor conservative news can proceed |url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/texas-lawsuit-claiming-us-helped-censor-conservative-news-can-proceed-2024-05-08/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240509043504/https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/texas-lawsuit-claiming-us-helped-censor-conservative-news-can-proceed-2024-05-08/ |archive-date=9 May 2024 |work=Reuters}}</ref> The [[Biden administration]] sought to have the case dismissed but federal judge [[Jeremy Kernodle]] agreed with the plaintiff and allowed the case to proceed.<ref name="Raymond-2024" /> The [[Second Trump administration|second Trump Administration]] later abolished the [[Global Engagement Center]], effectively ending the State Department's support for NewsGuard.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 Sep 2025 |title=Prompted by NCLA’s Suit, State Dep’t Comes Clean and Ends Scheme that Censored American Media |url=https://natlawreview.com/press-releases/prompted-nclas-suit-state-dept-comes-clean-and-ends-scheme-censored-american |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251219232412/https://natlawreview.com/press-releases/prompted-nclas-suit-state-dept-comes-clean-and-ends-scheme-censored-american |archive-date=19 December 2025 |access-date=19 Dec 2025 |website=[[The National Law Review]] (press release)}}</ref>

[[Brendan Carr (lawyer)|Brendan Carr]], who became [[Donald Trump]]'s appointee to the [[Federal Communications Commission]], accused NewsGuard of censorship and sent a letter to some tech companies to discourage them from working with NewsGuard. Some legal experts said that NewsGuard's opinions on sites' credibility are protected by the [[First Amendment to the United States Constitution|First Amendment of the Constitution]], and that the way Carr pressured private companies against working with NewsGuard raises First Amendment concerns. NewsGuard also replied that there were actually more conservative outlets it rated as credible than liberal ones.<ref name="Oremus-2024">{{Cite news |last=Oremus |first=Will |last2=Nix |first2=Naomi |date=December 24, 2024 |title=This company rates news sites' credibility. The right wants it stopped. |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2024/12/24/newsguard-disinformation-censorship-free-speech/ |newspaper=The Washington Post}}</ref> ''[[The Washington Post]]'' described NewsGuard's rating criteria as [[Nonpartisanship|nonpartisan]], writing that while fighting disinformation was still [[Bipartisanship|bipartisan]] when NewsGuard launched in 2018, disinformation watchdogs have since become a target of the Republican Party.<ref name="Oremus-2024" />
